title: Far from the madding crowd
summary: Far from the Madding Crowd is a pastoral novel set in the rural English county of Wessex, first published in 1874. It follows Bathsheba Everdene, a proud and independent young woman who inherits a farm and becomes its mistress, and the three men who vie for her affection. Gabriel Oak, a steady shepherd who loses his flock and fortune early in the story, works his way back up to become a farmer and remains devoted to her. William Boldwood, a reserved and wealthy bachelor, becomes obsessed with her after she sends him a playful valentine, and his passion turns dangerous. Sergeant Frank Troy, a dashing and unreliable soldier, wins her heart with charm and a romantic gesture, but his past and his weaknesses threaten her happiness. The novel moves through the seasons of farm labour, country festivals and local gossip, with a chorus of rural characters providing humour and commentary. Hardy explores pride, desire, duty and the consequences of impulsive choices, against a backdrop of changing rural life.
